newsitem.title: USA: Nu-Kote says ruling doesn't affect product.
newsitem.headline: Nu-Kote says ruling doesn't affect product.

text.p: Nu-Kote Holding Inc said Thursday a federal court's injunction prohibiting it from making and selling ink cartridges compatible with Epson America Inc's printers does not affect current products.
Epson, an affiliate of Seiko Corp, said earlier a Los Angeles federal court had issued an injunction against Nu-Kote's RF60, RF61 and RF62 cartridges.

Nu-Kote said in response that it redesigned its Epson- compatible inkjet cartridges "to avoid any issues in the lawsuit brought by Seiko-Epson" and that the injunction applies to an older models that have been discontinued.
The company added that it is currently shipping its redesigned inkjet cartridges and the court ruling has no impact on its current product line.

"The whole idea of these newly-designed cartridges is that they are designed around (Seiko-Epson's patents)," said Ronald Katz, the outside counsel for Nu-Kote. He added that Nu-Kote's suit against Epson, which alleges Epson violated anti-trust provisions, will proceed once the federal court in Los Angeles has ruled on all of Epson's patent claims.
Epson spokesmen could not not immediately comment on whether they will challenge Nu-Kote's redesigned cartridges.
Nu-Kote's stock fell 1/8 to 1-15/16 Thursday morning.
